units.la: AD STEPHANVM GERLACHIVM, ET ILLIVS ANTIDANAEVM
units.tr: To Stephen Gerlach, and His Anti-Danaeus

units.la: Lamberti Danaei necessaria responsio.
units.tr: Lambert Daneau's necessary reply.

units.la: ADuum Antidanæum, Stephane Gerlachi, virulenter quidem (quod omnes vident) in me scriptum, ipse tamen modeste responsurus, quoniam Laonici equitis vestri (qui prior in manus meas incidit, & erat aliquid istius equitis nobilitati certè tribuendum) argumenta iam confutaui, video neque durum, neque difficile mihi tecum restare certamen. Eadem enim est penè tuæ in me criminationis, quæ illius (& tamen utriusque falsæ) ratio, & audacia, & cum ξῦ πόδας ita secutus es, ut vel ille sua tibi dictasse, vel ipse ex Laonico tua transtulisse videaris. Est quidem mendaciorum, qualia sanè in utriusque vestrum scripto plurima continentur, ut plurimùm varia via, multiplex, & à seipsa dissentiens: veritatis autem via semper una, simplex, sibique consentiens: tamen, quum quid ex duorum, vel plurium inter se conspiratione suscipitur, mirum videri non debet, si inter illos aliquis consensus appareat. Sic enim in opprimêdo Christo testes illi duo, de quibus Matthæus scribit, conspiraverunt. Sic qui sanam Pauli doctrinam euertere conati sunt Iudæi, omnes inter se concordes apud Fœlice Syriæ Præsidé fuerunt, in cōfingendis, vt docet Lucas, aduersus Paulum criminationibus. Quo minus mirandum est, si Laonicus, & Gerlachius in eadem Tubingæ ciuitate versantes, eiusdem Scholastici cœtus & collegij membra, paria sui dogmatis propugnati præmia sperantes hactenus inter se consenserunt, vt me illi dogmati nequaquam assentientem, imò etiam illud oppugnante, iisdem confictis couitiis & telis confodere studuerint. Equidé quam primum duplex illud scriptum ad nos esset allatum, fere perterrebar. Nam statim occurrebat animo illud vetus, Ne Hercules quidem contra duos, verum postquam diligenter vtrumque recognoui, me ipsum collegi, & perspexi duos illos vna fidelia dealbatos parietes posse facile, nulloque negotio subuerti. Cum enim facta sit hæc scriptio ex argumento simplici duplex, certe qui vtramuis recte norit, ambas nouerit. Et mihi quidem animus primum fuerat vtrunque hunc coiungere, & iisdem vinculis colligare: verum ab aliquot, & meis, & istorū amicis monitus, asinum cum bove propter inæquale iugū nō esse copulandū, imò etiam, si id facere, eorum alterutrū præmio abOsiandro fore priuandū, ipsorum vtilitati, & cōmodis consules, atque illis amicis obsecut' Laonico, seu Nicodemo icntaculum, quod, vt opinor, illi satis erit, prius apposui: nunc autem & sua, vt loquitur Hieronymus, Cyprio boui dabitur merenda.
units.tr: Stephen Gerlach, I have read your Anti-Danaeus, written against me in a virulent spirit, as everyone can see, and I intend to answer it calmly. I have already refuted the arguments of your knight Laonicus, who came into my hands first and deserved some credit for his noble birth. I see that the contest with you will be neither hard nor difficult. Your accusation against me is almost the same as his, in its reasoning and its boldness, and you have followed him step by step [κατὰ πόδας], so that either he seems to have dictated your words to you or you seem to have copied yours from Laonicus. Lies of the kind found in great numbers in the writings of both of you are usually many-branched and varied, and they contradict themselves. The way of truth, however, is always one, simple, and consistent with itself. Still, when something is undertaken by two or more people in agreement, it should not seem strange if some harmony appears among them. Those two witnesses of whom Matthew writes agreed in their plot to destroy Christ. The Jews who tried to overturn Paul's sound doctrine were all of one mind before Felix, the governor of Syria, in fabricating accusations against Paul, as Luke tells us. It is less surprising, then, that Laonicus and Gerlach, who live in the same city of Tübingen and are members of the same scholastic company and college, hoping for the rewards due to the defenders of their own dogma, have so far agreed among themselves to attack me with the same invented insults and weapons, because I do not assent to that dogma and even oppose it. Indeed, as soon as that double writing reached me, I was nearly terrified. That old saying, "Not even Hercules can fight against two," immediately came to mind. But after I had read both carefully, I collected myself and saw that these two walls, whitewashed with the same plaster, could be easily and without any trouble knocked down. Since this writing is double but made from one simple argument, whoever knows one rightly knows both. My first intention was to join the two together and bind them with the same ties. But some friends, both mine and yours, warned me that an ass should not be yoked with an ox because of their unequal yoke; and that if I did so, one of them would be deprived of the reward from Osiander. Out of consideration for your own advantage and convenience, and to obey those friends, I have first set a morsel before Laonicus, or Nicodemus, which, I think, will be enough for him. Now, as Jerome says, the ox Cyprius will be given his due reward too.

units.la: Sic autem tibi,Gerlachi,respondebo,ut quae tibi cum Laonico nostro sunt communia,(sunt autem perplurima) ex meo ad eum scripto petere te velim,ne paginas,iisdem repetitis, impleam, & lectoribus crambe vestra bis apposita bis nauseam moveat. Quae etiam ex quarto V.Clarissimi Ioannis Sturmij Antipappo discere debebis,breuitatis gratia,omittam. Quae vero proprie tua sunt,nimirum diuturnam illam tuam inter modernos Constantinopolitanos (scis quid velim) moram plane redolentia, illa tantum hoc loco confutabo. Ecce igitur rem ipsam aggredior,& tuum scriptum,Gerlachi,examino.
units.tr: Gerlach, I shall answer you in this way. You may seek in my writing against him what you hold in common with our Laonicus, and there is a great deal of it. I will not fill pages by repeating the same things, nor make your readers feel sick at your cabbage served twice over. For the sake of brevity I will also omit what you should learn from the fourth Anti-Pappus of the most distinguished John Sturm. As for what is peculiarly yours, which smells of that long stay of yours among the modern Constantinopolitans (you know what I mean), I will refute only those points here. So now I approach the matter itself and examine your writing, Gerlach.

units.la: lampridem te meum Antiosiandrum accepisse,& in manibus habuisse,etiamsi nunc primum illi respondeas,significas. Prudentius profecto factum, quam ille vester Laonicus fecerit, qui intra quatriduum de re omnium maxima, nempe de Maiestate hominis Christi,de sacra Coena, de condemnandis tot Orthodoxis Ecclesiae Dei Pastoribus, intra pauxillum temporis (quorem tantam non potuit intelligere) respondendum sibi putauit. Tu vero catus homo recte vidisti, quam difficile,imo prorsus ἀδύνατον foret,veritati Dei a me propositae resistere, & tamen etiam in eo anteuertens Osiandrum (qui fortasis,omissis omnibus aulicis curis, mihi responsurus est)tam graue & durum certamen subiisti. Itaque hic te eodem nihilominus temeritatis crimine implicas,cuius ipsum Osiandrum & tu, & Laonicus damnastis, vtpote qui fateamini, non exspectato Pappi, aut alterius cuiusquam mandato, dato, nec explorata Pappi de non respondendo voluntate, magno ϕολυπεϱγμοσύνης vitio, in medium certamen vosmet vltrò proiecisse, & pro Pappo, non pro Argentoratensi Ecclesia respondisse. Lege igitur (si libet) quæ Laonico respondi. Nam quod me pro Sturmio respondisse, & illi suppetias, & auxilium scribis tulisse, ut Osiander Pappo tulit, erras toto cœlo. Liber enim meus est Apologia Doctrinæ Helveticarum Ecclesiarum, & professus sum, me, quicquid ad Sturmium, & Pappum, eamque concertationem Argentinensem pertinebat, omnino prætermissurum, quemadmodum etiam feci. Petis autem cur de Luca Osiandro breviter dixerim, ϰαϰὸν ϰόρακος ϰαϰὸν ὠὸν. Respondeo quoniam res ipsa sic habet. Etsi enim filius iste paternas hæreses omnes (quales sunt de essentiali Dei iustitia in quemlibet hominem infusa, de iustificationis nostræ causa, De Christo, qui etiam alicui naturam sumere potuerit, de confusa regeneratione cum iustitia, &c.) fortasse non sequitur: hanc tamen procul dubio paternæ similem retinet, ut asseueret, Humanitatem à λόγῳ assumptam, esse ipsius essentialis Deitatis λόγου Potentiæ participem, eiusque totam plenitudinem, in ipsam carnem Christi aut effusam esse, ut loquitur Iacobus Andreas, præceptor Osiandri vel communicatam, ut interpolavit Kemnitius. Item, quod ut pater Osiander, ita Filius Philippo Germaniæ lumini maledicit. Quid tu Gerlachi, qui tot regiones Turcicas peragrasti, tàdiu solus ignoras, quod longa rerum experien iá verisimum esse omnes didicerunt, Patrem fequitur {sua proles}? Sed ne diu squillas ex illo Osiadri patris sepulcro vellere me existimes, vel ex ipso Philippi testimonio, quod extat, qualis & quam impurus fuerit Osiander pater, cognosce, adeo ut, qui ex ea educatione & familia prodierit filius, vix bonus esse posse credatur. Nosti enim illud, Π αὐροι γαρ τοι πατρὶς ὁμοῖοι πατρὶ πλοῦτου, Οἱ πλέονες καὶ κακοὶ γενόμενοι πατρὸς ἀρετῆς.
units.tr: You say you received my Anti-Osiander long ago and had it in your hands, though you are only now answering it for the first time. That was certainly wiser than what your Laonicus did. Within four days he thought he had to answer on the most important matters of all: on the majesty of the man Christ, on the holy Supper, and on the condemnation of so many orthodox ministers of the Church of God, all within a very short time, which is not enough to understand so great a matter. You, however, clever fellow, rightly saw how difficult, indeed utterly impossible, it would be to resist the truth of God as I have set it forth. Yet even so, by getting ahead of Osiander (who will perhaps answer me once he has put aside all his courtly cares), you undertook so grave and hard a contest. Thus you still involve yourself in the same charge of rashness for which you and Laonicus condemned Osiander himself. You admit that, without waiting for a command from Pappus or anyone else, and without knowing Pappus's intention about not answering, you threw yourselves into the middle of the fight out of the great vice of busybodying [πολυπραγμοσύνη], and answered on behalf of Pappus, not on behalf of the Strasbourg Church. So read (if you like) what I replied to Laonicus. As for your claim that I answered on behalf of Sturm, and brought him help and aid, as Osiander did for Pappus, you are wrong by a whole sky. My book is the Apology for the Doctrine of the Helvetic Churches, and I declared that I would wholly pass over everything that pertained to Sturm, Pappus, and that Strasbourg dispute, as I indeed did. You ask why I spoke only briefly about Luke Osiander, "a bad egg from a crow" [κακὸν κόρακος κακὸν ᾠόν]. I reply that the matter itself stands thus. Although this son does not follow all his father's heresies (such as that the essential justice of God is infused into every man, the cause of our justification, the Christ who could take on a nature for anyone, the confused regeneration with righteousness, etc.), he undoubtedly keeps this one, which is like his father's: he asserts that the humanity assumed by the Word participates in the power of the essential Deity of the Word, and that the whole fullness of that Deity has been poured out into the very flesh of Christ, as Jacob Andreae, Osiander's teacher, puts it, or communicated to it, as Kemnitz has altered it. Likewise, just as Father Osiander curses, so the son curses Philip, the light of Germany. Gerlach, you who have travelled through so many Turkish regions, why do you alone remain so long ignorant of what all have learned from long experience to be true, that the offspring follows the father? But so that you do not think I am plucking squills from Osiander the father's grave, learn from Philip's own testimony, which still exists, what kind and how impure Osiander the father was, so that one can hardly believe a son who came from such an upbringing and family could be good. For you know that saying: "Few sons are like their fathers; most become worse than their father's virtue" [Παῦροι γάρ τοι παῖδες ὁμοῖοι πατρὶ πέλονται, οἱ πλείονες δὲ κακοὶ γινόμενοι πατρὸς ἀρέτην].

units.la: Quod autem Calvinum, Oecolampadium, Lutherum, & alios iam mortuos, laudavi, vide quo iudicio reprehendas, quasi ab illis vicissim laudem petam. Atqui, Gerlachi, mortui non loquuntur amplius, nec me laudare illi possunt. Itaque hic cessat illud, quod in me retorqueri posse putas, {Mutuo muli scabunt}. Sturmij quoque adhuc, Dei gratia, inter vos superstitis summas eruditionis laudes obiter attigi, quia vester praeceptor est, ut vos ipsos, si sanis illius consiliis acquiescceretis, multum proficere posse commonefacere. Quid-ni vero eum laudem, quem tu ipse laudas etiam inuitus? Num enim ab eo etiam laudari cupis? Quare nec hic quoque locum habere potest, {Mutuo muli}. Quanquam quid tibi venit in mente, ut modestissimum illud meum de Cl. V. Sturmio testimonium reprehenderes, quum eum virum universus orbis admiretur? Quod vero ais praeter vetustatis exempla à Sturmio (qui aliam artem, quàm Theologiam profitetur) Christianam religionem aduersus Eutychetis errore renovatum defendi, & ego variis exemplis iam refutaui, & tandem fateris ipse id eum facere potuisse. Certè sutor vltra crepidam non agit, quum Christianus Sturmius de Christiana religione, & filius de patris fui testamento disputat & quærit. Sed de Sturmio quæris, quæ fuerit illi obiecta necessitas veritatis aduersus Theses Pappi propugnandæ. Id verò disce tum ex superioribus Antipappis, tum ex luculentisimo illo quarto Antipappo, vbi manifestè docet mutatam esse à Pappo vetere illam, & orthodoxam Argentinensis Ecclesiæ fidei confessionem, quam ipsemet Pappus inter ipsas magistratus manus se perpetuò seruaturum esse iurauerat. Num verò Rectoris non interest, vt in Academia & vera pietas, & incorrupti professorum mores conseruentur? Quòd autè ipse à me Petri locum requiris, vbi docetur Christiani fidei suæ rationem cuiuis petéti redde re, in mei Antiosiádri margine annotaui, nec modò caput, sed & versiculũ ipsũ, ne vos propter fumos ceruisiarios, seu vinarios erraretis. Sturmiũ & omnes qui vestrum ambitiosum suggestũ non conscenderunt, fungos esse putas, Gerlachi, quasi tu in media Turcia ( vnde post diuturnam moram nunc primum redis) plus veræ Christi Theologiæ didiceris, quàm Sturmius, legendis assiduè veterum omnium orthodoxorum Patrum eruditissimis scriptis ( vt satis apparet) & quidem Argentinę, vbi florentissima fuit Dei Ecclesia? Audi verò tu qui titulum Doctoris tibi tribuis, Nemo, ait Gregorius, plus nocet in Ecclesia, quàm qui perverse agens, nomen vel ordinem sanctæ vitæ habet.
units.tr: As for my praise of Calvin, Oecolampadius, Luther, and others now dead, see with what judgment you blame it, as if I sought praise from them in return. But, Gerlach, the dead no longer speak, nor can they praise me. So the phrase you think can be turned back on me, "Mules scratch each other," has no place here. I have also touched briefly, by God's grace, on the highest praises of Sturm, who is still alive among you, since he is your teacher, to remind you that if you followed his sound counsels you could profit greatly. Why should I not praise the man whom you yourself praise, even unwillingly? Do you not wish to be praised by him too? So "Mules scratch each other" cannot apply here either. Yet why did it come into your mind to find fault with my most modest testimony about the most distinguished Sturm, when the whole world admires that man? As for your claim that, apart from examples from antiquity, Sturm (who professes an art other than theology) has defended the Christian religion renewed against the error of Eutyches, I have already refuted this with various examples, and in the end you yourself admit that he could do it. Certainly a cobbler does not go beyond his last, when a Christian, Sturm, disputes and inquires about the Christian religion, and a son about his father's testament. But you ask what necessity compelled Sturm to defend the truth against the Theses of Pappus. Learn this both from the earlier Anti-Pappi and from that most brilliant fourth Anti-Pappus, where he clearly shows that Pappus has altered that old and orthodox confession of faith of the Strasbourg Church, which Pappus himself had sworn in the hands of the magistrates that he would always keep. Surely it is in the interest of the Rector that both true piety and the uncorrupted morals of the professors be preserved in the academy? As for your request that I point out to you the place in Peter where it is taught that one must give an account of one's Christian faith to anyone who asks, I have noted it in the margin of my Anti-Osiander, not only the chapter but the verse itself, so that you would not err because of the fumes of beer or wine. Gerlach, do you think Sturm and all who have not climbed your ambitious platform are mushrooms, as if you, in the middle of Turkey (from which you have only now returned after a long stay), had learned more of the true theology of Christ than Sturm, who has constantly read the most learned writings of all the orthodox Fathers, as is clearly evident, and that in Strasbourg, where the Church of God flourished? Listen, you who claim for yourself the title of Doctor: "No one," says Gregory, "does more harm in the Church than one who, acting perversely, has the name or the rank of holy life."

units.la: Ergo vos, qui vobis solis claues scientiæ retinere vultis, & neminem ad eam intrare sinitis, plus nocetis Ecclesiæ, quàm qui nullo D. Doctoris, & D. Superintendentis titulo & fastu turgidus, candide fidei suæ rationem inter Christianos exponit. Quod fecit Sturmius, & quidè rectisimè. Nam ecquis Christianus paulò eruditior, sic falso prætudicio est præoccupatus, ut vestra, & Sturmij scripta legens, Sturmium infinitis partibus, etiam in Theologicis, & te ipso, (qui fortasse centes magnum quendam esse te Theologum) & Pappo, & Osiandro doctiorem esse non statim iudicet, & videat? Quis sis enim & quantus, vel ex eo apparet, quòd quum negarem Apollo, Aquilam, Andronicum, Iuniam, & similes alios fuisse ex illorum duodecim Apostolorum numero, statim collegisti, Ergo eosdem Theologiam quoque, ex mea sententia, neque didicisse, neque tractasse. Quasi ego aut quisquam Christianus eruditior, idem sentiat quod tu, idem esse nimirum Apostolum esse, & Theologiæ, ac fidei Christianæ scientem. Imò nec quicunque verus Christianúsque Theolog' est, propterea, vestro more, Episcopus est, & Superintendens, vel etiam alia artem palàm exercere, & profiteri prohibetur: quod tamen in Sturmio stultè culpas. Nisi fortasse Paulum ipsum,selectu illud Dei organum, Corinthi morantem, & illic οικονομίαν exercentem, tunc Theologum non fuisse, aut perperam egisse censes. Et quid tibi venit in mentem, ut in Dei Ecclesia, atque etiam temporibus ipsius Pauli Apostoli, Priscillam illam mulierem etiam inter Pastores & Doctores fuisse, ex Dorotheo fortasse tuo, autore nihili, vel potiùs ex tetra Pepuzianorum hæresi scriberes? Num quæso publicè mulieres in Ecclesia docent in Turcia, vbi tandiu
units.tr: Therefore you, who wish to keep the keys of knowledge to yourselves alone and allow no one to enter, do more harm to the Church than the man who, puffed up with no title of "Doctor" or "Superintendent" and no pomp, candidly sets out the reason of his faith among Christians. This is what Sturmius did, and quite rightly. For what Christian of any learning is so possessed by false prejudice that, reading your writings and Sturmius's, he does not at once judge and see that Sturmius is infinitely better, even in theology, than you (who perhaps think yourself some great theologian), and than Pappus and Osiander? What sort of man you are, and how great, appears even from this: when I denied that Apollos, Aquila, Andronicus, Junia and similar others were among the number of the twelve apostles, you at once inferred, "Therefore, by your opinion, they neither learned nor practised theology." As if I, or any more learned Christian, held your view, namely that to be an apostle is the same as to be versed in theology and the Christian faith! Nor is every true Christian theologian, by your custom, made a bishop and superintendent, or forbidden to practise and openly profess some other art; yet you foolishly blame Sturmius for this. Unless perhaps you think that Paul himself, that chosen instrument of God, while staying at Corinth and there exercising the "oikonomia" [οικονομίαν], was not a theologian then, or acted wrongly. And what came into your head, that you should write, perhaps from your Dorotheus, an authority worth nothing, or rather from the foul heresy of the Pepuzians, that in the Church of God, and even in the time of the Apostle Paul, that woman Priscilla was among the pastors and teachers? Do women, I ask, teach publicly in the Church in Turkey, where you were so long?

units.la: Act. 11 v. 3. & 10. v. 4. 1. Cor. 9. Pag. 13. tandiu fuisti? Sed etiam si inter eos fieret, tamen in Christiana Dei Ecclesia fieri non debet: neque, se viuo, fieri vnquâ certè passus esset Paulus, vtcunque eam συνεργὸν suam vocet, quam tu, Theologe, vocem, etsi Theologicam, non intellexisti. D. autem Sturmius, quem Theologum esse negas, rectè sanè intelligit. Sed neque falsò contra Vbiquitatem, vt Cresconius contra Augustinū, scripsit: imò verè, & orthodoxè, quem admodum Arnobius, & Minutius, ipsi Grammatici; de Christiana religione libris etiâ editis, disputarunt: contra Vbiquitatem, inquam, vestram, & nouam, & veterem. Nouam quidem si vocem spectes, veterem autem propter erroris fundamentum. Itaque toto coelo aberras, dum putas & nos, & Sturmium nolle vt errores, qui modò verè sunt errores, damnentur: imò homines etiam ipsos errantes, si modò perseuerarint, legitimè auditos & conuictos damnamus. quod vos facere negatis velle: & tamè Laonicus imprudens, & arcanum suorum iam prodens, vos velle, & eò spectare, mihi in Spongia indicauit. Quare iam tibi non erimus Cyclopes & Epicurei, quum & errores, (qui verè sunt errores) & personas ipsas errantes, prius auditas, & conuictas, & nihilominus obstinatè perseuerantes, damnemus, quemadmodum audis. Quæris autem, iterum & sæpiùs, quid fuerit necesse vt Sturmius patrocinium veritatis contra Theses Pappi susciperet. Ad id ego verò iam respoderam, Gerlachi. Sed quia, quemadmodum video, quid agas, non attendis, denuò quoque respondeo, Quia veritas à Pappo oppugnabatur, quia technis, & doctis, vt ait ille,dolis petebatur,qui sunt vi aperta dam nabiliores: quia & sana & vetus Argentinensis scholæ fidei confessio à Bucero, Capitone,toto Senatu comprobata, & in quam omnes professores iam olim iurauerant,mutabatur:quia deni que aliter ipse Pappus sui sacramenti immemor, erat peieraturus. Quod in ipsiusmet Pappi commodum pati noluit Sturmius, Argentinensis Academiæ Rector,ad quem professorum omnium, vti dixi,inspectio,& morum constitutio pertinet. Vides igitur quàm necessaria fuerit caussa Sturmio tot peccatorum ab Argentinensi ciuitate auertendorum, propter quæ ira Dei venit in homines, quemadmodum Paulus ait. Caeterum σαρκικὸν φαρμακον est, quod & à te, & à vestris affertur, non totas Ecclesias nostras à vobis damnari, sed tantùm nos earum Pastores.Quiculas enim ipsas excipi scribis. Atque nulli sunt in nostris Ecclesiis, qui prudentes ac scientes Vbiquitatem vestram non reiiciant, & veram de sacra Domini Cœna doctrinam, quam annuntiamus, non libenter, & προαιρετικῶς animi certissima & deliberatissima amplectantur. Sed nimirum magna est vestra hæc sapientia, & astutia, qui, vt ouibus nostris,& grege ipso toto postea facilius potiamini, Pastores earum eiicere (pacis cum grege ineundæ praetextu) desideratis. Nimirum vti astutus ille Athenarum hostis,Philippus Macedonum Rex, optimos quosque viros expulit Athenis,quos & Rheto-
units.tr: Act. 11 v. 3. & 10. v. 4. 1. Cor. 9. Pag. 13. Yet even if it happened among them, it ought not to happen in the Christian Church of God; nor would Paul, while he lived, ever have allowed it, however much he calls her his synergos [συνεργὸν], a word you, theologian, did not understand, though it is a theological word. Doctor Sturmius, whom you deny to be a theologian, understands it quite rightly. Nor did he write falsely against Ubiquity, as Cresconius wrote against Augustine; rather he wrote truly and orthodoxly, just as Arnobius and Minucius, the grammarians, disputed about the Christian religion in books that were published; against your Ubiquity, I say, both new and old. New if you look at the word, but old on account of the foundation of its error. So you are wholly mistaken when you think that we and Sturmius do not want errors, which truly are errors, to be condemned. Indeed we condemn men themselves who err, if they persevere after being lawfully heard and convicted. You deny that you wish to do this; yet the unwary Laonicus, already betraying the secrets of your party, has shown me in the Sponge that you do wish it and aim at it. Therefore we shall not now be Cyclopes and Epicureans to you, since we condemn both errors (which truly are errors) and the erring persons themselves, first heard and convicted and nevertheless obstinately persevering, as you hear. You ask again and again why it was necessary for Sturmius to take up the defence of truth against the Theses of Pappus. To this I had already replied, Gerlach. But since, as I see, you do not attend to what you are doing, I answer again: because truth was being attacked by Pappus; because it was being sought by tricks and learned wiles, as he puts it, which are more dangerous than open force; because the sound and ancient confession of faith of the Strasbourg school, approved by Bucer, Capito and the whole Senate, and to which all the professors had long ago sworn, was being altered; and because Pappus himself, forgetful of his oath, was about to perjure himself. Sturmius, rector of the Strasbourg Academy, to whom, as I said, the oversight of all the professors and the regulation of morals belongs, was unwilling to allow this even for Pappus's own advantage. You see then how necessary a cause there was for Sturmius to turn Strasbourg away from so many sins, on account of which the wrath of God comes upon men, as Paul says. Moreover, you and yours bring forward a fleshly remedy [σαρκικὸν φαρμακον], namely that you condemn not all our churches but only us, their pastors; for you write that the little sheep themselves are excepted. And there are none in our churches who, being prudent and knowing your Ubiquity, do not reject it, and who do not gladly embrace the true doctrine of the Lord's Supper that we proclaim, with a deliberate choice [προαιρετικῶς] and the most certain and considered judgement of mind. But your wisdom and cunning is surely great, you who wish to expel their pastors (under the pretext of making peace with the flock) so that afterwards you may more easily get hold of our sheep and the whole flock. Just as that crafty enemy of Athens, Philip king of Macedon, drove the best men out of Athens, whom he also called rhetors,

units.la: Ephef.5.
units.tr: Ephes. 5.

units.la: Pag.16. & 17. Rheroras, & seditiosos, vt tu Sturmium facis, appellabat. Verum quid tibi faciam, qui vestrum illud Damnare idem esse atque nostru ne-ges? quasi vos dogma duntaxat, no personas: nos autem & dogma & personas legitime conuictas, & obstinate perseuerantes damnemus. Atqui primum a Laonico tuo, id est, collegij tui dignissimo membro refutaris, qui ab Osiandro, & a vobis, & nos & nostrum dogma simul damnari affirmat, adeoque nos a vobis ipsi magistratui tradi, vt saltem grauissima illa exilij poena multemur. Quod nisi nobis istud arcanu fuoru prodidisset Laonicus, futura scilicet erat grauis de eo controuersia. Sed tuipse tande teipsum destruis, & quod dico verum esse, & ab Osiadro fieri, pag. 19.20.21. agnoscis. Age igitur, & cum tuo collegio, & tecum ipse consenti, Gerlachi. Deinde res ipsa, quam exercetis, aliud omnino probat. Quot enim patriis sedibus expulistis? quot quotidie expellitis? quot expellere adhuc cogitatis, & in carceribus detinetis? Fortasse tibi, qui tandiu patria caruisti, & plus terrarum, quam vilus mulio pedes petuarius calcasti, neque exilium, neque carceres inter poenas iam censentur: sed in eo contra commune omnium hominum sensum iudicas. Haec vero & Pappana, & Osiandrica, & iam Gerlachiana distinctio, vt haeresis damnetur, intacto tamen manente haeretico, qui in ea perseuerat, ferri sustinerique nullo modo, quemadmodum docui, potest. Itaque, quum eam meram esse stropham, Illustrissimi Principes, qui etiam vobis fauerant, intelligerent, coegerunt vos, quanquam inuitos, tollere illud vestrum & superbum,& arrogans Damnamus, & anathematizamus. Conquereris etiam quòd vestram sententiam non capiam, quia dixi personas errantes,& perseuerantes, vnà cum dogmate à vobis necessariò damnari,quicquid id vos facere negetis. Excipis enim tu belle, non omnes personas sic errantes à vobis damnari,sed ouiculas excipi. Atque hæc quæ iam dicam,tua sunt,quę etiam ad oues perseuerantes in errore pertinent,nimirum vt generaliter omnes persona conuiƈta, admonita, & tamen pertinaciter hærefin retinentes, damnentur.Ergo & oues, vti & Pastores, ex teipso sunt damnandæ. Vides quid velis.Præterea quæro ex te,si toti greges nostri vestram Vbiquitatem (de qua iam audierunt) detestantur, & ex animi,non autem(vt vestri putant)ex vlla ignoratione vestræ sententiæ, vestrarúmque rationú(quas nô dissimulamus illis) nostram doctrinam de Cœna amplectuntur, vestram prorsus reiiciunt: nónne iam erunt tibi damnandi etiam greges ipsi toti? Certè erunt. Atque antea responderá, tales esse nostros greges, vt iam inter nos ouiculas tuas Vbiquitarias frustra quæras, ideóque nostras totas Ecclesias,quicquid simules,dissimulé suè,condemnas. Quod autem Zuinglium, & Caluinum ab orthodoxis damnatos ais,profer vel vnum,qui id fecerit,& viceris. Sed magno animi errore falsum pro vero sumis,& Vbiquitarios appellas orthodoxos, id est, principium in probando petis. Vt & Laonicus, qui Vbiquitariam doctrinam vocat Catholicam,cum & à nostris ftris,& à Papistis adeò ipsis oppugnetur & expugnetur ex Dei verbo.Quod porrò addis,Peccatores conuerti posse, & nos concedimus. Quis enim hoc nescit? Itaque erroris prius volumus legitimè conuinci, qui vt hæretici damnantur,& tamè diu tolerari : ac etiam propterea bene de vobis speramus, etsi grauissimè nunc erratis, quoniam illud nobis est notissimum, Nemo desperet melior a lapsis.Denique vos tandem nostram sententiam amplexuros speramus, id est, veritati assensuros.Paulus ex lupo, & Saule factus est Paulus,& Christi Apostolus:Cyprianus ex mago, & Augustinus ex Manichæo factus est Christianus. Sed dum de damnandis hominibus agimus,non de iis intelligimus, de quibus adhuc spes est: sed deiis,de quibus desperatur,siue sint illi Pastores, siue greges & ouiculæ, quòd nimirum in iis omnis,vt ad resipiscendum adducerentur,via verbo Dei præscripta, & more maiorum, id est,Ecclesiastico constituta,tentata,& obseruata fuerit. Solos enim eos damnandos dicimus: vos autem semper occinitis,Pastores, non ouiculas.Nec à nobis, ais,in vestris Ecclesiis præter Pastores ipsos quisquam damnatur. Hæc non cohærent,quoniam etiam eæ, quas appellas,Ouicula perstant, ex vero animi proposito, in nostra ea doctrina, quam vos damnatis: & nobiscum vestras rationes & dogmata certo animi iudicio, publicè priuatímque omnes, & singulæ illæ ouiculæ reiiciunt. Ergo singulæ, & omnes à vobis damnantur: atque ita totæ Ecclesiæ nostræ à vobis anathematizantur. Atque vtinam etiam tu verum diceres, quum addis, de conuictis tantum illam personarum damnationem intelligi. Nam saltem in nobis Pastoribus damnadis illud expectaretis, & seruaretis, vt falsæ doctrinæ conuinceremur. Verum nimia odij in nos cæcitate omne legitima agendi ratione prætermittitis, de quo iam pridem coquerimur. Sed vt vident omnes, surdis ista canimus. Sed quid plura? Tu enim ipse Gerlachi, omni iam metu nos liberas. Nam si, vt tu ais, Ea fidei confessio, quæ per vim obtruditur, vel verborum blanditiis persuadetur, nullo modo totius Ecclesiæ confessio putanda est, & qui falsorum doctorum clamoribus adducti, eam amplectantur, non sunt hæretici: certè iam neque Nouæ vestræ doctrinæ Nouum corpus confessio, totius Ecclesiæ Dei Germanicæ confessio censenda est, neque nos, qui eam non amplectimur, hæretici iudicandi. Quis enim ignorat, quo astu, quibus verborum lenociniis, quibus policitationibus, imo etiam qua via, & quibus minis subscriptiones illorum, maxima ex parte clericorum (qui illam confessionem nouam subsignarunt) fuerint à volaterrano illo Iacobo Andrea, & alijs extortæ, & erusca? Quis nescit vestrorum doctorum, qui errorem Eutychianum reuocant, clamoribus hoc ipsum Nouæ vestræ doctrinæ corpus populis inuitis obtrudi? Ergo pulchrè te ipsum, & tuam illam concordiam hac tua sententia condemnas, & de gradu deiicis: & nos absoluis: quandoquidem tantum ipsius veritatis vis apud te potuit, vt hæc abs te inuito extorqueret.
units.tr: Pag. 16. & 17. and seditious men, as you do with Sturmius. But what am I to do with you, who deny that your Damnare is the same as our condemning? As if you condemned only the doctrine and not the persons, while we condemn both doctrine and persons, lawfully convicted and obstinately persevering. Yet first you are refuted by your own Laonicus, that most worthy member of your college, who affirms that both we and our doctrine are condemned by Osiander and by you, and that we are handed over by you to the magistrate so that at least we may be punished with that most grievous penalty of exile. If Laonicus had not betrayed this secret of yours, there would certainly have been a serious dispute about it. But you yourself at last destroy yourself, and you acknowledge that what I say is true and is done by Osiander (pp. 19, 20, 21). Come, then, Gerlach, agree with your college and with yourself. Next, the very thing you practise proves something altogether different. How many have you driven out of their homelands? How many do you drive out every day? How many do you still plan to expel, and keep in prisons? Perhaps to you, who have been so long without a homeland and have trodden more lands on foot than a common mule-driver, neither exile nor prisons are now counted among punishments; but in this you judge against the common sense of all men. This distinction of Pappus, of Osiander, and now of Gerlach, that heresy should be condemned while the heretic who persists in it remains untouched, cannot, as I have shown, be endured or upheld in any way. Therefore, when the most illustrious princes, who had also favoured you, understood that this was a mere trick, they compelled you, though unwilling, to drop that proud and arrogant Damnamus and anathematizamus. You also complain that I do not grasp your view, because I said that persons who err and persevere must necessarily be condemned by you together with the doctrine, whatever you deny. For you neatly make an exception: not all such persons are condemned by you, but the little sheep are excepted. Yet what I now say is yours, and pertains also to the sheep who persevere in error, namely that generally all persons convicted, admonished, and yet pertinaciously retaining heresy are to be condemned. So the sheep, as well as the pastors, are to be condemned by your own account. You see what you want. Besides, I ask you: if all our flocks detest your Ubiquity (of which they have already heard), and embrace our doctrine of the Supper from the heart, not from any ignorance of your opinion and arguments (as your people think, though we do not hide them from them), and utterly reject yours: will not you then condemn the whole flocks as well? Surely you will. Earlier I answered that our flocks are such that you will search in vain for your Ubiquitarian sheep among us; so, whatever you pretend, you condemn our whole churches, whether you dissemble or not. As for your claim that Zwingli and Calvin were condemned by the orthodox, produce even one who did so, and you will have won. But with a great error of mind you take the false for the true, and you call the Ubiquitarians orthodox, that is, you beg the question. So too Laonicus calls the Ubiquitarian doctrine Catholic, though it is attacked and overthrown from God's word by our people and by the Papists themselves. As for your further addition, Sinners can be converted, we also concede it. For who does not know this? Therefore we wish first to have error lawfully convicted; and if it is condemned as heresy, yet has been tolerated for a long time, we hope well of you too, even though you now err most gravely, since this is most well known to us: Let no one despair of those who have fallen. Finally, we hope that you will at last embrace our view, that is, assent to the truth. Paul was made from a wolf, and Saul became Paul, Christ's apostle; Cyprian was made from a magician, and Augustine from a Manichaean, a Christian. But when we speak of men to be condemned, we do not mean those of whom there is still hope, but those who are despaired of, whether they are pastors or flocks and little sheep: namely, those in whom every way prescribed by God's word and the custom of our forefathers, that is, established by the Church, has been tried and observed, to bring them to repentance. For we say that only those are to be condemned; but you keep singing Pastors, not sheep. Nor, you say, is anyone condemned by us in your churches except the pastors themselves. These claims do not cohere, since even those you call sheep persevere, from a sincere purpose of mind, in that doctrine of ours which you condemn; and all of them, singly and together, publicly and privately, with a certain and settled judgement of mind, reject your views and doctrines. Therefore each and every one is condemned by you, and so all our churches are anathematized by you. Would that you spoke the truth also when you add that the condemnation of persons is to be understood only of those convicted! For at least in condemning us pastors you would wait for and observe that we were convicted of false doctrine. But through excessive blindness of hatred towards us you neglect every lawful way of proceeding, about which we have long complained. But, as everyone sees, you sing these things to the deaf. Yet why say more? For you yourself, Gerlach, now free us from all fear. For if, as you say, That confession of faith which is forced upon men, or persuaded by flattery of words, is in no way to be considered the confession of the whole Church, and those who embrace it, led on by the clamours of false teachers, are not heretics: then certainly the confession of your new doctrine cannot be regarded as the new body of the whole Church, the German confession of God's Church, nor are we, who do not embrace it, to be judged heretics. For who does not know by what cunning, with what verbal enticements, what promises, indeed by what way and with what threats, the signatures of those (mostly clergy) who subscribed that new confession were extorted and wrung out by that Volaterran, Jacob Andreae, and others? Who does not know that your teachers, who revive the Eutychian error, force this very body of your new doctrine upon unwilling peoples with clamours? So you beautifully condemn yourself and your concord by this opinion of yours, and cast it down from its place; and you absolve us, since the force of truth itself has been so strong with you that it has wrung this from you against your will.

units.la: Pag.16. Ea fidei confessio ... non sunt hæretici queret. Caeterum quod negas inter primos huius controuersiae disceptatores (non autem inter vos & nos) de verbis potius, quàm de rebus certamen fuisse, id & Pappus ipse in re- sponsione sua ad Sturmium fallus est, & ita diserte aperteque ex eorum scriptis demonstrauì, vt tu totum tuae refutationis praesidium τῷ ὑποφάνω, id est, in mera negatione quaesieris, quia verissima testimonia à me prolata refutare nullo modo poteras. De quo ipso quoniam iam in Laonico dixi, ad ea te remitto, & ad Epistolam Caluini tum ad Philippum, Quan-quam, 141. tum ad Marbachium tuum, quem ad hoc infoelix certamen agendum cohortaris. Iam fere, 147. & ad quartum Antipappum Sturmij praeceptoris tui, & ad teipsum, pagina 33. & 34. Caeterum eadem fide superiora negas, qua contendis nullam fuisse mutuam inter Caluinum, Philippum, Bucerum, Capitonem, Oecolampadium, Viretum, & caeteros nostros amicitiam, quae tamen ex eorum epistolis luce meridiana clarius & certius apparet: sed tuae occupationes eas legere, quanquam à me citatas, non sinunt: nec commentarium Philippi, vbi ille apertissime nostram sententiam de carne Christi in coelum recepta, & ibi contenta vsque ad diem iudicij, probat, & confirmat. Nam quòd ais, Oecolampadium appellasse signa S. Coenae, symbola carnem Christi corporalis praesentiae modo absentem repraesentantia, Lutherum vero dixisse, carnem ipsam Christi exhiberi, & idcirco eos inter se de reipsa dissensisse, hoc ipsum te refutat. Ostendit enim de re quidé ipsa, id est, de carne Christi( quòd detur in S. Coena) fatis inter eos conuenisse : sed de modo præsentiæ certamen mansisse,quum Lutherus corporalem, Oecolampadius autem spiritualem carnis Christi præsentiam esse,per fidem nimirum,coñ tenderit. Quæ Oecolampadij sententia procul dubiò est verissima,& ipsi Sacramentorum naturæ omnino consentanea. Lutherus igitur suas phrafes , Oecolampadius item suas retinebat: Denique quod à Luthero Vbiquepræfentiam probatam esse dicis, facis Osiandro magnam iniuriam, qui eam tam procul,vt infaustam,& inauspicatan auem (& merito quidem)à fe suisque ædibus abegit.A vobis ascensionem Christi mutari in euanefcentiam, seu disparentiam carnis Christi in his nubibus & aere, vbi tamen adhuc versatur,sed inuisibilis nobis,quum dico,Gerlachi,non mentior.Sie enim loquuntur postremæ Theses Andreæ Musculi, qui vnus fuit ex ipsis Nouæ doctrinæ sex compilatoribus, & fabricatoribus. Et certè illud omnino ex vestra Vbiquitate, velitis nolitis, consequitur. Cur verò conquereris, quasi non suam carni Christi maiestatem tribuamus, cùm eam & corde & ore affirmemus esse supra cœlos omnes excelsissimos eue&tam, & ad Patris omnipotentis dextram sedentem,& gloria ipsis beatis Angelis admirabili habitualiter etiam ornatam:imò eam esse vnicum illum vitæ æternæ ab ipsa λόγῳ Deitate in nos deriuandæ canalem,electum & datum nobis à Deo, cui nos communicare omnino oporteat, vt vitæ illius æternæ succum ex ipso Christo, Filio Dei, hauriamus? Quid amplius igitur à nobis desideras? Nempe vt humanam naturam à λόγῳ assumptam ipsi naturæ assumenti, id est, Deitati, Maiestatica vestra chimæra, exæquemus, id quod vos nomine Maiestatis, & omnipræsentiæ carnis Christi fi aperte facitis. Verum sic de Christi carne, etiam glorificata, sentire, non est ex Dei verbo sapere: sed ex Eutychetis delirio blasphemare.
units.tr: Pag. 16. That confession of faith ... they are not heretics, you complain. But as for your denial that the first disputants in this controversy (I mean, not between you and us) fought over words rather than things, Pappus himself is wrong about this in his reply to Sturmius. I have shown this so plainly and openly from their writings that you, unable to refute the very true testimonies I cited, have had to seek your whole defence in mere denial [τῷ ὑποφάνω]. Since I have already dealt with this point in the Laonicus, I refer you to that, and to Calvin's letter to Philip, Quanquam, p. 141, and to your Marbach, whom you urge on to this unhappy contest, Iam fere, p. 147, and to the fourth Antipappus of your teacher Sturmius, and to yourself, pp. 33 and 34. Yet you deny the earlier points with the same good faith with which you maintain that there was no mutual friendship between Calvin, Philip, Bucer, Capito, Oecolampadius, Viret and our other friends, a friendship which nonetheless appears from their letters more clearly and certainly than the noonday sun. But your occupations do not allow you to read them, though I cited them, nor Philip's commentary, where he most plainly proves and confirms our view that the flesh of Christ, received into heaven, is contained there until the day of judgement. As for your claim that Oecolampadius called the signs of the Lord's Supper symbols representing the flesh of Christ, which is absent in the manner of a bodily presence, while Luther said that the flesh of Christ itself is exhibited, and that for this reason they disagreed with each other about the thing itself, this very point refutes you. For it shows that they did agree sufficiently about the thing itself, that is, that the flesh of Christ is given in the Supper; the dispute remained only about the mode of presence, since Luther held the presence of Christ's flesh to be bodily, and Oecolampadius held it to be spiritual, that is, through faith. Oecolampadius's view is beyond doubt the truest, and wholly in agreement with the nature of the sacraments. So Luther kept his phrases and Oecolampadius kept his. Finally, when you say that the ubiquity of the presence was approved by Luther, you do a great wrong to Osiander, who drove it away from himself and his household as an unlucky and ill-omened bird, and rightly so. You say that by us the ascension of Christ is changed into a vanishing, or a disappearing of the flesh of Christ into these clouds and air, where nonetheless it still dwells, but is invisible to us. When I say this, Gerlachius, I do not lie. For the last theses of Andreas Musculus, who was one of the very six compilers and makers of the New Doctrine, say so. And indeed this follows necessarily from your ubiquity, whether you like it or not. But why do you complain, as if we did not ascribe majesty to the flesh of Christ, when we affirm with heart and mouth that it has been raised above all the highest heavens, sits at the right hand of God the Almighty, and is adorned habitually with a glory wonderful even to the blessed angels; indeed that it is that single channel of eternal life, chosen and given to us by God, from the Deity of the Word [λόγῳ] through which that Deity flows into us, and with which we must necessarily communicate, so that we may draw the sap of that eternal life from Christ himself, the Son of God? What more, then, do you want from us? Clearly, that we should make the human nature assumed by the Word equal to the nature that assumes it, that is, to the Deity, by your majestic chimera, which you plainly do under the name of majesty and omnipresence of the flesh of Christ. But to think this way of the flesh of Christ, even glorified, is not to know wisely from the Word of God; it is to blaspheme from the madness of Eutyches.

units.la: Cæterum quam suauis & facetus es, mi Gerlachi, dum tuæ Vbiquitati præsidiū ab ipsis apostatis, & Antitrinitariis, (quos, siqui alij, maximè oppugnamus) contra nos quæris? nempe nisi huiusmodi hereticorum testimoniis fulciretur vestra illa Vbiquitas, erat statim ruitura. Ergone nos nostramque doctrinam ex vnius istius apostatæ Neuferi literis, abs te fideliter scilicet descriptis, grauare belle cogitas? Sed primùm, vt tibi de literis istis credamus, quid illæ contra nos? Imò docent, quandiu inter nos ille vixit, nec talem fuisse, quem Constantinopoli vidisti: nec, nisi à nobis, nostráque doctrina fugeret, talem vnquam futurum fuisse. Sumúsne vero ex eo damnandi, quòd qui apostatæ à vera fide fieri volunt, neque inter nos diutius versari, neque tolerari possunt? Ecquis nescit in ipsa Christi familia, & Apostolorum cœtu Iudam proditorem fuisse? ex ipsa Christiana & Apostolica Ecclesia, & Nicolaum, & Cerinthum, & Philetum, & Hymenæum, & reliquos omnes Hæreticos extitisse? Estne propterea doctrina ipsa Apostolica
units.tr: Yet how charming and witty you are, my dear Gerlachius, when you seek protection against us from the apostates themselves and the Antitrinitarians (whom we oppose more than any others)! Surely without the testimonies of such heretics your Ubiquity would at once collapse. Are you really planning to burden us and our doctrine with the writings of that single apostate, Neuferus, which you have faithfully copied out? But first, let us grant that we may trust those writings: what do they say against us? Indeed they teach that while he lived among us he was not such a man as you saw at Constantinople, and that he would never have become such a man had he not fled from us and our doctrine. Yet do we incur blame because those who want to become apostates from the true faith can neither remain among us any longer nor be tolerated? Who does not know that Judas the traitor was in the very household of Christ and the company of the Apostles? That Nicolaus, Cerinthus, Philetus, Hymenaeus and all the other heretics arose from the Christian and Apostolic Church itself? Is the Apostolic doctrine therefore to be condemned, or are the Apostles themselves, its heralds, to be burdened with any hatred or prejudice and stained with any blemish? Rather, from this very fact their purity, both of doctrine and of the Church, is seen, because among them, just as among us, there are no more heresies...

units.la: H.j. damnanda, vel ipsi Apostoli illius praecones vl-lo odio & praejudicio gravandi, & vlla labe com-maculandi? Imò verò ex eo potius ipso puritas eorum, & doctrinae, & Ecclesiae animaduertitur, quòd inter eos, vti & inter nos, non magis vllae haereses aut Apostasiae sordes, quàm foeda aliqua spuma in medio pelago, conquiescere potest, sed longè in littus aliquod, & extra eiiciatur necesse est. Itaque idem tibi respondemus, quod ipse Iohannes Christi Apostolus, quibusdam tui similibus, hypocritarum ab Evangelio ad haeresin, aut paganismum defectiones Ecclesiae exprobrantibus respondit, Ex nobis egressi sunt, sed non erant ex nobis. Nam si fuissentex nobis, permansissent. Sed hoc factum est, vt patefieret non omnes esse ex nobis. Caeterum quod à Neusero dictum maiusculis literis, tanquam Apollinis oraculum, nobis notasti, Qui timet sibi ne incidat in Arrianismum, caveat Calvinismum,vt ab illo siue dictum, siue scriptum, vel potius à te fuisse confictum tibi concedam, & hac criminatione impurus ille sibi onerandos eos putarit, quos Heidelbergae suae blasphemiae inimicissimos fuit expertus: quàm fide dignus est hic Apostata tuus, & quidem vnicus testis? Denique, quis non animaduertit illum infelicem, tum sui purgandi, tum infamandae doctrinae totius Christianae causa, atque vt ita optimum illum, & illustrissimum Principem Fridericum Tertium, Comitem Palatinum, traduceret, ista facile effutisse? apud te praesertim, huiusfhuiusmodi falsos rumusculos, etiam aduer- sus Germanos Principes, auidè Constantino- poli à quouis, ( vt ex tuis ad Cythraeum literis apparet ) captante idque potuisse. Ergo tui ob- lectandi gratiâ hæc dixerit, vel scripserit Nau- ferus, quem non ignorabat esse nostræ confef- sionis hostem infestissimum, & à tua sodalita- te eò missum, vt ipse secundus à Iacobo An- drea Vbiquitatis Apostolus Græcos, & Con- stantinopolitanum Patriarcham, ad tuam fi- dem, si posses, conuerteres, & in vestrum er- rorem induceres. Sed ille Græcus haud natus in veruecum(vt aiunt)patria,& te Germano na- sutior,techna s, & odores tuos olfecit,& sibi ma- turè à tuo errore cauit. Itaque turpissimam ab eo repulsam passus,reliquum temporis vagus & iners illic vixisti, fuitque tota hæc tua legatio inanis, quoniam te non satis aptum legatum tuus ille conuentus delegerat: adeò quidem, vt etiam quædam Græcorum vocabula in chartis collegeris, quorum explicationem & significa- tionem per M. Crusium, à viro doctiss. Fran- cisco Porto collega meo(id quod verè affirmo) emendicare te non puduerit, vt multum prose- cisse in ea peregrinatione videreris, & alienis, id est,F. Porti veluti plumis ornatus, te tuis vendi- tares. Intellextin' qui sis, Gerlachi, & vt tua Tur- cica discursatio sit nobis nota? & ad tua quidem Turcica testimonia tibi sic resposum esto. Quòd autè esse ιλαβολον criminaris, quod dixi, Sacramenta lem & Spirituale carnis Christi man ducationem
units.tr: Or should the apostles themselves, their preachers, be burdened with hatred and prejudice and stained by any blemish? Rather, their purity, both of doctrine and of the Church, is shown by this very fact: among them, as among us, no heresies or stains of apostasy can settle any more than some foul scum can settle in the middle of the sea. It must be cast out far onto some shore. So we give you the same answer that the apostle John himself gave to certain people like you, who taunted the Church with the defections of hypocrites from the Gospel to heresy or paganism: "They went out from us, but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would have remained. But this happened so that it might be made plain that not all are of us" (1 John 2:19). As for what you have noted, in capital letters, from Neuserus, as if it were an oracle of Apollo: "Whoever fears for himself lest he fall into Arianism, let him beware of Calvinism." Suppose I grant that he said or wrote this, or rather that you yourself invented it, and that in this slander that foul man thought to burden those whom he had found most hostile to his blasphemies at Heidelberg. How trustworthy is this apostate of yours, and indeed your only witness? Finally, who does not see that this wretched man blurted out such things, both to clear himself and to defame Christian doctrine as a whole, and so to slander that excellent and most illustrious prince Frederick III, Count Palatine? He could easily do so, especially before you, who eagerly took up such rumours of this kind, even against the German princes, from anyone at Constantinople (as appears from your letters to Chytraeus). So Neuserus said or wrote these things to please you, though he knew that I was a most bitter enemy of our Confession, and that he had been sent there by your fellowship, so that, like Secundus, second to Jacob Andreae, the apostle of ubiquity, you might convert the Greeks and the Patriarch of Constantinople to your faith, if you could, and draw them into your error. But that Greek, not born, as they say, in the land of rams, was sharper-nosed than you, a German, and sniffed out your wiles and your stench, and took early care to guard himself against your error. So, having suffered a most shameful rebuff from him, you lived the rest of your time there idle and aimless, and this whole embassy of yours came to nothing, since that assembly of yours had chosen you as an unsuitable envoy. Indeed, you collected some Greek words in your papers, and you were not ashamed to beg their explanation and meaning from Martin Crusius, and from the most learned man, my colleague Francis Portus (which I affirm to be true), so that you might seem to have made much progress on that journey, and might sell yourself to your own people adorned with the feathers of others, that is, of Francis Portus. Do you understand, Gerlach, who you are, and how your Turkish wanderings are known to us? As for your Turkish testimonies, let this be my reply to you. But as for your charge that I am a slanderer [διάβολον] because I said that the sacramental and spiritual eating of Christ's flesh

units.la: H.ij. ab Osiandro, velut res inter se pugnantes, committi, in eo me non calumniatum esse, sed verum scripsisse affirmo. Nam verba & manducationem spiritualem à Christo commemorata cap. 6. Iohannis, ad eiusdem carnis manducationem, in S. Coena, nequaquam accommodari vel pertinere posse, ubique ille in toto illo suo Antisturmio, & tu pag. 45. quoque, & tui omnes (salsissime tamen) contendunt, ne convincantur sacrum & essentiale Christi corpus alio instrumento, quàm fide & spirituali sumi. Quare eas duas manducationes eiusdem essentialis carnis Christi, inter se, vt αὐτημίνας, & Osiander (quod dixi) & tui (quod non percipis) inter se opponunt. Videntigitur omnes, me non esse διάβολον: sed te, quae extuis, tuorumque verbis necessario consequuntur, non intelligere. Nam quod ait Osiander, necessarium esse, vt etiam in Coena spiritualiter caro Christi manducetur ab eo, qui suam salutem promouere velit, non vult ille, ipsam Christi carnem in S. Coena, non, nisi spirituali fidei ore, sumi posse, quandoquidem hic idem ad Gallicas Ecclesias scripsit, ipsam carnem Christi etiam impuro indignorum ore sumi posse: sed hoc vult ille nimirum, ne cogatur fateri, etiam locum Iohannis, (qui modum explicat, extra quem essentialis Christi caro manducari nullo modo potest) etiam de manducatione verae carnis Christi, quae fit in S. Coena, intelligi quoque oportere: ac illam repugnantiam, quam dixi, inter sacramentalem & spiritualem verae Christi carnis manducationem à vobis constitutam tollere videatur. Quòd autem me irrides, qui inter Credere & manducare cam distinctionem constituam, quae est inter caussam instrumentalem, & effectum, tu potius mihi homo, vere teipsum deridendum omnibus propinas, qui causas & effecta salutis secernere non potes. Sed quia de eo ad Laonicum iam respondi, illinc, si libet, responsum pete. Porro nouam hic nobis inuidiam conflare conaris. Vis enim sacramentalem ipsius carnis Christi manducationem a nobis non tantum confundi cum spirituali (quod tui nobis antea obiiciebant) sed eam omnino a nobis tolli, quoniam non concedimus essentialem Christi carnem in S. Coena ore corporis manducari. Qua in re prorsus falleris. Sacramentalis enim verae & essentialis Christi carnis manducatio est ea, qua Sacramentalem actionem celebrantes, & signorum vsum adhibentes, veram Christi carnem, solo fidei, non corporis, ore percipimus, quam nos & fatemur, & agnoscimus. Itaque una & eadem semper est verae carnis Christi manducatio, non diuersa, siue in Coena Domini, siue extra Coenam fiat, &ea semper vno & eodem instrumento, nempe fide, fit a nobis? In adiunctis tantum discrimen est, quod nimirum in Sacramentis, ad nostrae fidei confirmationem, signa quaedam a Deo instituta adhibentur: extra Sacramenta vero nullus est eiusmodi visibilium signorum vsus. Tu vero, Capernaitarum more, sentis in S.Coena aliter, & alio iustrumento ipsam essentialem Christi carnem edi: aliter, & alio instrumento extra S Coenam. Sed in eo falli te dicimus. Vnius enim, & eiusdem Sacrosanctae carnis, Christi edendæ vnicum duntaxat, & perpetuum semper est instrumentum, nempe fides, vbicunque illa caro edatur, siue in Sacramentis, siue absque Sacramentis. Vides igitur, vt neque tol-lamus Sacramentale ipsius carnis Christi mandu-cationem, sed tu Sacramentalem interpretaris man-ducationem carnali modo, siue ore corporis fa-ctâ, ipse carnalis: neque eam cum mere spirituali manducatione cofundamus, vt ad vtrâque tuam in nos calumniam habeas verisimum meum re-sponsum. Sed vide, quàm ipse ineptias, qui spiri-tualem manducationem definias pag. 49. eam, qua non ipsum corpus Christi, sed eius beneficiatan-tum percipimus. Agnoscisne tua verba Gerlachi? Quòd verò me parente, & præceptore (neque enim me meorum præceptorum, vt te tuorum, velut Philippi, pudet) meo P. M. Ioanne Caluino inui-diosè perspicaciore facis, quum dico, Ioā. locum, 6. cap. generaliter de manducatione carnis Chri-sti, siue in Cœna, siue extra Cœnā accipi, & non ad solam Cœnā restringi, vide quid Caluinus ipse & ibidē, & alibi scripserit. Nā hoc quoque quod dixi, me ab illo didicisse facile cognosc es. Ille e-nim fatetur in cap. 6. Iohannis, nihil dici, quod non in Cœna figuretur. Itaque sacram Christi Cœ-nam huius concionis sigillum esse scribit. Vides igitur ab ipso Caluino abstergi illud scomma, quo scur-riliter aspergere me conatus es. Cæterùm quæ à pag. 47. vsque ad 51. continentur, ex superioribus sunt satis confutata. Vnū modò obseruan-dum est, Gerlachium vi veritatis victum tandem acquiescere nostræ sententiæ, cùm fateatur con-tra omnium suorū opinionem, ipsummet Chri-
units.tr: I affirm that I have not misrepresented Osiander when I say that the spiritual eating of Christ, which John 6 describes, is set against the eating of the sacramental body, as though they were things at odds with each other. I have written the truth. For the words of John 6 and the spiritual eating they describe cannot be applied or related to the eating of that same flesh in the Holy Supper. Osiander throughout his whole Antisturmius, and you too on page 45, and all your people (very wittily, I grant), insist that the holy and essential body of Christ must not be received by any means other than faith and spiritual eating. So Osiander, as I said, and you, though you do not grasp it, set these two eatings of the same essential flesh of Christ against each other as opposites [αὐτημίνας]. Everyone can see, then, that I am not a διάβολος, but that you do not understand what you say and what your own words necessarily imply. For when Osiander says that it is necessary for anyone who wishes to promote his salvation to eat the flesh of Christ spiritually even in the Supper, he does not mean that the flesh of Christ can be received in the Supper only by the spiritual mouth of faith. The same man wrote to the churches of France that the flesh of Christ itself can be received even by the defiled mouth of the unworthy. What he means, of course, is this: he does not want to be forced to admit that John's passage, which explains the mode outside of which the essential flesh of Christ cannot in any way be eaten, must also be understood of the eating of the true flesh of Christ that takes place in the Holy Supper. He wants to remove the contradiction I mentioned, which you have set up between the sacramental and the spiritual eating of the true flesh of Christ. As for your mockery of me for drawing a distinction between believing and eating, which is the distinction between the instrumental cause and the effect, you yourself, sir, are the one who ought truly to be laughed at by everyone, since you cannot separate the causes of salvation from its effects. But since I have already answered that point to Laonicus, look there for my reply if you wish. Furthermore, you are trying to stir up a new hatred here. For you want to charge that we not only confuse the sacramental eating of the flesh itself with the spiritual eating (which your people objected to us earlier), but that we abolish it altogether, because we do not grant that the essential flesh of Christ is eaten in the Supper by the mouth of the body. In this you are wholly mistaken. For the sacramental eating of the true and essential flesh of Christ is that by which we, celebrating the sacramental action and making use of the signs, receive the true flesh of Christ by the mouth of faith alone, not of the body; this we both confess and acknowledge. Thus there is always one and the same eating of the true flesh of Christ, not a different one, whether it takes place in the Lord's Supper or outside it, and it is always made by us through one and the same instrument, namely faith. The only difference lies in the circumstances: in the sacraments, certain signs instituted by God are used to confirm our faith, whereas outside the sacraments there is no use of such visible signs. But you, after the manner of the Capernaites, think that in the Supper the essential flesh of Christ is eaten in one way and by one instrument, and outside the Supper in another way and by another instrument. In this we say you are wrong. For there is only one instrument, and always the same, for eating that one and the same most holy flesh of Christ, namely faith, wherever that flesh is eaten, whether in the sacraments or without them. You see, then, that we do not abolish the sacramental eating of the flesh of Christ; rather, you interpret the sacramental eating in a carnal way, as something done by the mouth of the body, and so are yourself carnal. Nor do we confuse it with a merely spiritual eating, so that you have no ground for your calumny against us, and you see that my answer is true. But look how foolishly you yourself go on, when on page 49 you define spiritual eating as that by which we receive not the body of Christ itself but only its benefits. Do you recognise your own words, Gerlachius? As for the fact that you have sneered, with more spiteful sharpness than is fair, at my father and teacher (for I am not ashamed of my teachers, as you are of yours, such as Philip), my Pater Magister John Calvin, when I say that John 6 speaks generally of the eating of the flesh of Christ, whether in the Supper or outside it, and is not restricted to the Supper alone, see what Calvin himself has written both there and elsewhere. For you will easily recognise that I learned this point from him as well. He admits in chapter 6 of John that nothing is said there that is not figured in the Supper. So he writes that the holy Supper of Christ is a seal of this sermon. You see, then, that Calvin himself wipes away the jibe with which you tried to spatter me scurrilously. As for what is contained from page 47 to page 51, it has been sufficiently refuted from what has been said above. There is only one thing to note: Gerlachius, overcome at last by the force of truth, agrees with our opinion, since, contrary to the view of all his own people, he admits that Christ himself is eaten in the Holy Supper not by sacramental eating alone but only when spiritual eating is joined to it. So this man is almost on our side on page 53, when he says that the sacramental eating of the flesh of Christ is a sealing of the spiritual eating of the same flesh. From this I gather, even on Gerlachius' own testimony, that the flesh of Christ is eaten in the Supper in no other way than outside the Supper. This is true, it agrees with us, and it openly opposes his own people.
